To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed and tested a high-throughput genotyped platform for apple SNP markers.
we identified 37,807 SNP markers from 6888 apple EST sequences.

we have developed a high-throughput SNP genotyping platform that can be applied to a broad range of apple genotypes, including wild species, and that this platform can be used to identify SNPs associated with traits of interest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of SNPs from ESTs of 14 diverse apple cultivars and their validation using the GoldenGate genotyping assay.
developing an apple SNP genotyping assay that will be useful for high-throughput genomics and marker assisted selection (MAS) in apple breeding programs.
the identification of SNPs from ESTs of apple, the development of a custom GoldenGate™ assay, and genotyping of apple cultivars and wild species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
44% of the identified SNPs are valid SNPs, and 56% are either invalid, paralogous or both.
60% (841 SNPs) of the SNPs tested were validated, while the other 26% (366 SNPs) might be derived from duplicated regions.
60% SNPs are reliable SNPs, 26% are paralogous SNPs, and 14% SNPs are invalid SNPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a total of 12 299 SNPs from 6525 contig sequences were identified and 1411 SNPS were genotyped.
10,000 SNPs are available for genotyping apple germplasm using the GoldenGate assay.
a high-throughput genomics platform has been established to genotype apple germplasm using the Illumina GoldenGate™ assay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a large number of high quality SNPs can be identified in apple EST sequences.
the GoldenGate assay can be a powerful tool for high-throughput genotypic analysis in apple and other species with large and complex genomes.
the use of GoldenGate assay is an efficient tool for genotyping a large number of SNPs in apple.
